title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.
key_points: RL with verifiable rewards (math, code) drives reasoning ability without heavy supervised fine-tuning.
An early RL-only experiment (R1-Zero) spontaneously developed reflection and chain-of-thought behaviors.
Full R1 combines a small amount of supervised fine-tuning with large-scale RL for stable, readable output.
Reasoning traces from R1 can be distilled into compact models that punch well above their parameter count.
Released openly, matching or approaching o1-level math and reasoning performance.
content_html: DeepSeek-AI released R1 in January 2025, an open reasoning model that acquires strong chain-of-thought reasoning primarily through reinforcement learning rather than large amounts of supervised demonstrations. The paper also introduced distilled smaller variants that inherit R1's reasoning style.
extra_html:
How it works

The authors first trained R1-Zero using only RL with verifiable reward signals (correctness on math and code problems). Remarkably, this model spontaneously developed reflective reasoning and self-correction in its traces. Full R1 adds a small cold-start supervised phase before RL to stabilize output format. The resulting reasoning traces were then used to fine-tune smaller dense models via distillation.

Why it matters

DeepSeek-R1 validated that reasoning capabilities are not locked behind proprietary training pipelines: open RL on verifiable tasks gets you most of the way there. The distillation finding is especially practical - teams can get strong reasoning in a 7B or 14B model without training from scratch. Dig into the paper on arXiv for the full ablations and training recipe.

related.title: OpenAI o1: Learning to Reason with Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: OpenAI's o1 lets a model think via a long internal chain-of-thought before answering - spending more compute at inference time visibly improves reasoning.

related.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
related.hook: Ask a big model to 'think step by step' and its math and logic scores jump. Reasoning was there all along — you just had to ask it to show its work.

related.title: PPO: Proximal Policy Optimization
related.hook: Reinforcement learning is notoriously unstable. PPO's fix is simple: never let a single update move the policy too far. That restraint made it the field's workhorse.

related.title: VibeThinker-3B: Frontier Reasoning in a Small Model
related.hook: A 3B model matches giant flagships on hard math and coding - because verifiable reasoning, it turns out, compresses into a tiny 'reasoning core.'
